prompt: How many people wrote the Agile Manifesto in 2001?
"Working software over comprehensive documentation." What does the manifesto say about the documentation?

choices.text: It has value
choices.why: Right: the manifesto ranks, it does not reject.

choices.text: It should be abolished
Only testers may write it
It must be written before any code, in full detail, and signed by the customer
choices.why: That is closer to the waterfall.

prompt: "Working software is the primary measure of progress." What does that imply for testing?
hint: Somebody has to know it works.

choices.text: Progress is measured by how many test cases have been written so far in the cycle
It shows progress
choices.why: Right: every couple of weeks, somebody establishes it works.

choices.text: Testing becomes unnecessary
Only the final release is tested

prompt: Why does "responding to change" have a cost the testing side pays?

choices.text: Testers are paid by the change
Change is forbidden in testing
Each change requires a new tester to be hired for the team
Tests must change as fast as the requirements they check
choices.why: Right: a team that cannot change its tests has stopped being able to change.

hint: Build eight days, test on the ninth.

choices.text: A sprint where building fills eight days and testing is squeezed into the last two
choices.why: Right: the waterfall shrunk to two weeks.

choices.text: A small waterfall project
choices.why: It is about sprints in agile teams.

choices.text: A sprint of one day
Testing on each day of the sprint, beginning with questions on day one
choices.why: That is the version that works.

prompt: Which habits make continuous testing possible, by this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: small stories
a shared definition of done
automated regression checks
a testing phase at the end of each sprint

prompt: "The whole price rule" is too big for a story. Why does size matter to testing?

choices.text: A small story reaches testing early, alone, while its author remembers it
choices.why: Right: "students pay half" is a story.

choices.text: Big stories cannot be tested
Small stories need no testing
Size decides how much the team charges the cinema for it

prompt: "Short cycles make every defect a young defect." Why is that only true if testing keeps pace?

choices.text: Young defects are harder to find
It is true either way
choices.why: Not if testing waits for the end.

choices.text: A defect waiting untested until the cycle ends ages like any other
choices.why: Right: the mini-waterfall throws away the benefit.

choices.text: Defects age faster in sprints than in a waterfall, whatever testing does

prompt: Match each Cine Aurora test to its quadrant.
hint: Support or critique; business or technology.

pairs.left: "a student on Wednesday pays R$ 18,00", written with Joana
three hundred buyers on opening night

prompt: What are the two axes of the agile testing quadrants?

choices.text: Manual or automated; fast or slow
Developer or tester, depending on who runs each of the tests on the team
choices.why: The lesson says the map is not about who.

choices.text: Before release or after
Support or critique; business or technology

prompt: A heavily automated team has full Q1 and Q2 and nothing in Q3. Why is that typical?

choices.text: Automation covers Q3 automatically
Q3 can only be done by the customer at the very end of the project, after release
Exploring produces no green tick
choices.why: Right: the map exists to show that empty corner.

choices.text: Q3 is not allowed in agile
choices.why: It is part of the map.

prompt: The Wednesday stacking was found by exploring and then written as an example with Joana. Which quadrants did it move between?
hint: Found by exploring, kept by automating.

choices.text: It stayed in Q3
choices.why: Written as an example, it moved.

choices.text: From Q3 to Q2
From Q1 to Q4, as it was automated
choices.why: Neither is about examples or exploring.

choices.text: From Q2 to Q3
The licence cost of a testing tool, paid in instalments
Unchecked work
choices.why: Right: it compounds like technical debt.

choices.text: Money owed to testers
Tests that fail

prompt: What usually happens to teams that never automate regression checks, by the lesson?

choices.text: They become a waterfall team by choice
They hit a wall
choices.why: Right: re-testing by hand outgrows a cycle.

choices.text: Nothing changes
They hire one more tester every sprint until the regression pile shrinks again

prompt: A tester learns what a story means on the day it is handed over. What is the team running, by this lesson?

choices.text: A spiral
Behaviour-driven development, where examples come after the code has been written
A mini-waterfall wearing agile vocabulary, with the tester left out of the first conversation
choices.why: Right: lesson 5’s gate with new furniture.

choices.text: Proper Scrum
choices.why: The tester belongs in the first conversation.

prompt: A rule changes three times in a cycle. What defence does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Write each answer as an example
choices.why: Right: then change is deliberate and visible.

choices.text: Refuse to test until it settles
Ignore the changes
choices.why: The tests would check the wrong rule.

choices.text: Ask for a longer cycle so that the rule has time to stop changing
